To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best results for anomaly detection in large, high-resolution, grayscale aerial images of a forest with uniform background are obtained using the RXD with the local intensity difference as input feature.

the Reed-Xiaolidefender (RXD) classifier with the local range as feature is the best choice for anomaly detection of man-made objects in large, high-resolution grayscale aerial images with relatively uniform background.

(1) the RXD classifier performs well in this application, (2) local intensity range performs well as a feature, (3) hard negative mining is not required in this application and (4) the local binary patterns feature performs poorly in this application.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RXD with local intensity range gives good performance, and that it is a viable alternative to the more expensive and computationally complex SVM.

a combination of the RXD classifier and the local intensity range features is the most suitable for the anomaly detection of small man-made objects in large grayscale aerial images with a uniform background.

the RXD is a promising candidate for the detection of man-made objects in uniform, grayscale aerial images.
the choice of classifier and features is important, and that the choice of the best performing classifier and feature set depends on the application and the type of data.
